evidence.claim: Article 110 gives the Leader supreme command of the armed forces, war-and-peace authority, and appointment power over key judiciary, media, and military posts; Article 111 provides a temporary replacement council if the office becomes vacant.
evidence.title: Iran (Islamic Republic of) 1979 (rev. 1989) Constitution
evidence.excerpt: Article 110 gives the Leader supreme command of the armed forces, war-and-peace authority, and appointment power over key judiciary, media, and military posts; Article 111 provides a temporary replacement council if the office becomes vacant.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Stable constitutional text reproduced by a reputable legal repository; directly defines authority and constraints relevant to 2022.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Direct office-level authority held by Ali Khamenei as Supreme Leader.
contrary_evidence: The constitution includes a formal vacancy-replacement mechanism, so the office is powerful but not literally unbounded on paper.

evidence.claim: Iran's Revolutionary Guards claimed responsibility for a dozen ballistic missiles fired at Erbil; the attack was presented as retaliation for an Israeli air raid in Syria, and Kurdish authorities said a civilian was injured.
evidence.title: Iran attacks Iraq's Erbil with missiles in warning to U.S., allies
evidence.excerpt: Iran's Revolutionary Guards claimed responsibility for a dozen ballistic missiles fired at Erbil; the attack was presented as retaliation for an Israeli air raid in Syria, and Kurdish authorities said a civilian was injured.
evidence.source_locator: article body, paragraphs describing the attack and casualties
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Reuters wire report with contemporaneous attribution and casualty reporting.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Directly attributable to Iran's state security apparatus under Khamenei's ultimate authority, though not a personal order transcript.
contrary_evidence: IRGC framed the strike as retaliation, not aggression.
No American personnel were hurt, so the immediate material harm was limited relative to later 2022 attacks.

evidence.claim: The SRSG said Iran's missile attack on Erbil killed civilians, including a little girl, but also noted that Iraq and Iran were engaged in dialogue and did not wish to escalate the issue.
evidence.title: Briefing to the Security Council by SRSG Jeanine Hennis-Plasschaert
evidence.excerpt: The SRSG said Iran's missile attack on Erbil killed civilians, including a little girl, but also noted that Iraq and Iran were engaged in dialogue and did not wish to escalate the issue.
evidence.source_locator: lines 101-105 and 127-130 of the briefing text
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Primary UN field-mission briefing, contemporaneous and directly specific to the attack and the diplomatic context.
evidence.period_fit: Direct 2022 follow-up to the March attack
evidence.ruler_attribution: The attack is attributed to Iran within the UN diplomatic record; that is a state-action attribution under Khamenei's authority rather than a personal speech transcript.
contrary_evidence: The same briefing acknowledges ongoing Iraq-Iran dialogue, which is the main restraint/peace point in the 2022 record.
This is a diplomatic briefing, not a legal finding on command responsibility.

evidence.claim: Iran's Revolutionary Guards launched artillery attacks on Iranian militant opposition bases in northern Iraq and said the operations would continue to ensure border security and punish terrorists.
evidence.title: Iran's Guards launch artillery attack on militants in Iraqi Kurdistan
evidence.excerpt: Iran's Revolutionary Guards launched artillery attacks on Iranian militant opposition bases in northern Iraq and said the operations would continue to ensure border security and punish terrorists.
evidence.source_locator: article body, quoted IRGC statement and surrounding paragraphs
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Reuters wire with direct operational attribution and the Guards' stated rationale.
evidence.period_fit: Exact 2022 event during the Mahsa Amini protest wave
evidence.ruler_attribution: Directly attributable to the IRGC under Iran's top security hierarchy, which Khamenei ultimately oversees.
contrary_evidence: The official rationale is a self-serving security claim, not independent proof of necessity.
The targets were opposition bases in another sovereign state.

evidence.claim: Reuters reported that Iran's Revolutionary Guard said it fired 73 ballistic missiles at Kurdish opposition groups in Iraq; Iraqi Kurdish authorities said at least nine civilians were killed and dozens were wounded.
evidence.title: Iran says it fired 73 ballistic missiles at Kurdish groups in northern Iraq
evidence.excerpt: Reuters reported that Iran's Revolutionary Guard said it fired 73 ballistic missiles at Kurdish opposition groups in Iraq; Iraqi Kurdish authorities said at least nine civilians were killed and dozens were wounded.
evidence.source_locator: article body and casualty summary near the headline sections
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Reuters feed with explicit numerical and casualty claims from the same-day attack.
evidence.period_fit: Exact 2022 event at the height of the protest crackdown
evidence.ruler_attribution: Strongly attributable to the IRGC under Khamenei's strategic authority, even if the decision chain is not laid out in the article.
contrary_evidence: Iran framed the strike as counterterrorism against Kurdish militants.
Casualty counts varied across local reports, so the exact death toll is not perfectly settled.

evidence.claim: Iran's foreign minister said a small number of drones had been supplied to Russia months before the February 24 invasion and denied continued supply, while Reuters noted Russia had used the drones against power stations and civilian infrastructure in Ukraine.
evidence.title: Iran acknowledges drone shipments to Russia before war, Kyiv says Tehran is lying
evidence.excerpt: Iran's foreign minister said a small number of drones had been supplied to Russia months before the February 24 invasion and denied continued supply, while Reuters noted Russia had used the drones against power stations and civilian infrastructure in Ukraine.
evidence.source_locator: article body around the foreign minister's quoted remarks
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Reuters wire carried contemporaneous acknowledgement from Iran's foreign minister, which is unusually direct evidence.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Indirect but strong attribution through Iran's foreign minister speaking for the regime under Khamenei's authority.
contrary_evidence: Iran denied that the transfers continued into the war.
The report does not prove a direct Khamenei order or timing beyond 'months before' the invasion.

evidence.claim: The Council said three Iranian individuals and one Iranian entity were sanctioned because of their role in the development and delivery of UAVs used by Russia in its war against Ukraine.
evidence.title: Ukraine: EU sanctions three individuals and one entity in relation to the use of Iranian drones in Russian aggression
evidence.excerpt: The Council said three Iranian individuals and one Iranian entity were sanctioned because of their role in the development and delivery of UAVs used by Russia in its war against Ukraine.
evidence.source_locator: opening paragraphs of the press release
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Primary EU sanctions text, explicit about the reason for designation and the Russia-Ukraine context.
evidence.period_fit: Exact 2022 sanctions response to the drone issue
evidence.ruler_attribution: Attribution is to Iranian state-linked actors, not directly to Khamenei personally, but the action sits inside the system he heads.
contrary_evidence: Sanctions target listed persons/entities, not the Supreme Leader by name.
The EU press release is a legal-political response, not a forensic finding on the entire chain of command.

evidence.claim: Treasury said firms were involved in the production or ongoing transfer to Russia of Iranian UAVs that Russia used in attacks on civilian infrastructure in Ukraine, and identified Shahed Aviation Industries Research Center as responsible for Shahed-series UAV production.
evidence.title: Treasury Targets Actors Involved in Production and Transfer of Iranian Unmanned Aerial Vehicles to Russia for Use in Ukraine
evidence.excerpt: Treasury said firms were involved in the production or ongoing transfer to Russia of Iranian UAVs that Russia used in attacks on civilian infrastructure in Ukraine, and identified Shahed Aviation Industries Research Center as responsible for Shahed-series UAV production.
evidence.source_locator: opening section and the 'Iranian UAV Producer' section
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Primary U.S. sanctions notice with concrete findings, named entities, and mission-specific details.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Indirect attribution to the IRGC aerospace ecosystem under Khamenei's rule.
contrary_evidence: This is a sanctions determination by the U.S., not an international adjudication.
It names firms and the IRGC aerospace force, not Khamenei personally.

evidence.claim: Reuters reported that rockets and drones hit Iranian Kurdish party headquarters in Iraqi Kurdistan, killing at least two people and wounding ten, and said the Revolutionary Guards had been attacking dissident bases since the Mahsa Amini protests began.
evidence.title: Iran strikes dissident sites in Iraqi Kurdistan, two dead - officials
evidence.excerpt: Reuters reported that rockets and drones hit Iranian Kurdish party headquarters in Iraqi Kurdistan, killing at least two people and wounding ten, and said the Revolutionary Guards had been attacking dissident bases since the Mahsa Amini protests began.
evidence.source_locator: article body around the casualty count and IRGC attribution
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Reuters wire with same-day reporting and direct attribution to the Guards.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Strongly attributable to the IRGC under Khamenei's security hierarchy.
contrary_evidence: Iran described the targets as terrorist groups and framed the operation as security-related.
This is still a media report, not a judicial finding.
